preconditions.description: The number of test cases is between 1 and 100 inclusive.
For each test case, the string length n is between 2 and 100, and the number of queries q is between 1 and 100.

preconditions.expression: len(s) == n and all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s has length n and contains only '0' and '1'.

preconditions.expression: 1 <= l_i < r_i <= n for all queries (l_i, r_i)
preconditions.description: Each query consists of two integers l_i and r_i such that 1 ≤ l_i < r_i ≤ n.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join(['YES' if any(len(set([i for i in range(1, n+1) if s[i-1] == s[l_i-1 + k] for k in range(len(sub)) if i != l_i-1 + k and all(i < j for j in [i for i in range(1, n+1) if s[i-1] == s[l_i-1 + k] for k in range(len(sub)) if i != l_i-1 + k])])) >= 2 and sub == ''.join([s[i-1] for i in sorted([i for i in range(1, n+1) if s[i-1] == s[l_i-1 + k] for k in range(len(sub)) if i != l_i-1 + k])]) else 'NO' for l_i, r_i in queries]) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each query (l_i, r_i), the output is 'YES' if there exists a good subsequence in s that matches the substring s[l_i...r_i], otherwise 'NO'. A good subsequence is non-contiguous and has length ≥ 2.
